build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player controls a boat with smooth 2D movement using keyboard, mouse, or both; the boat visibly turns or glides through water in response to input with acceleration or responsive directional control. Score 0 if the boat is static, teleports, or cannot be steered.

Collision or slowdown prevents the boat from sailing through islands, docks, harbor edges, or obstacles. The replay shows navigation meaningfully constrained by the environment. Score 0 if the boat passes through all obstacles freely.

Picking up cargo visibly changes the boat's HUD loadout or sprite and marks cargo as carried. The pickup state persists and affects the next delivery action. Score 0 if pickup is invisible or does not alter game state.

Delivering matching cargo to the correct customer grants coins, stars, or reputation and clears the order. Destination matching is observable — wrong destinations reject or ignore the delivery. Score 0 if deliveries are cosmetic or any destination accepts any cargo.

Multiple orders with timers or priorities create route-planning pressure; at least one urgent order is observable. Choosing order sequence or route matters for outcome. Score 0 if orders have no timing or priority difference.

A top-down harbor map is navigable with water lanes, docks, islands or obstacles, pickup points, customers, and route markers that constrain or guide play. Score 0 if the map is empty or not navigable.

At least three distinct customers or destinations are visible with different cargo needs, icons, colors, locations, or rewards, and the distinctions affect delivery choices. Score 0 if all deliveries go to one generic point.

At least one multi-stop, capacity, or sequencing decision is demonstrated: carrying multiple parcels, limited cargo capacity, choosing order sequence, or balancing urgent jobs. The decision affects reward, timing, or outcome. Score 0 if every delivery is isolated with no planning.

An upgrade or planning screen offers at least three choices (speed, cargo capacity, tip bonus, route hints, or similar) and choosing one visibly changes later play. Score 0 if there is no upgrade or planning layer.

Victory and failure or low-rating result screens show deliveries, earnings, rating, missed orders, and retry/title controls. Results reflect prior delivery performance. Score 0 if results are missing.
A styled title screen shows the game name, Start button, harbor art, and courier boat identity before gameplay begins. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.

The flow connects title or scenario -> harbor shift -> pickup/delivery play -> upgrade/planning or result screen without restarting the executable. The delivery loop is playable end to end. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.

The HUD shows current cargo, active orders, destination hints, earnings, and shift timer or remaining time in clear non-overlapping regions. The player can read delivery status at a glance. Score 0 if route and delivery status are hidden or absent.

Readability at 1280x720 is strong: boat, obstacles, cargo, customer icons, order timers, route hints, and HUD are distinguishable and do not overlap or become ambiguous. Score 0 if navigation or order state is unreadable.

The harbor art direction is coherent and cozy across title, water, docks, boat, cargo, customers, route lines, HUD, upgrades, and results. A consistent palette, typography, iconography, spacing, and visual hierarchy hold the game together at a publishable vertical-slice standard. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The harbor environment uses real sprite or tile art for water, docks, islands, and buoys — not plain ColorRect fills or default HTML 引擎 primitives. Different map elements are visually distinct and recognisable. Score 0 if the environment is uniform color fills or unstyled rectangles.

HUD and UI chrome: cargo indicators, order panels, timer displays, upgrade menus, and result screens use styled themed widgets (custom panels, icon buttons, illustrated frames, or themed StyleBox), not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Numeric text uses a custom or styled font. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled default default widgets or if chrome treatments differ wildly between screens.

Animation and feedback are present: boat wake or ripple, pickup pop, delivery sparkle or chime visual, timer warning pulse, route marker animation, or coin/rating changes use tween, particles, or motion rather than instant snaps. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently with no animation.
